subject: API latency incident — status update & mitigation
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@concordiahealth.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: Status page update: Intermittent API latency affecting hosted inference — investigating

Alex —

Quick update from our side: we observed a spike in API latency across the hosted inference fleet starting ~06:55 PT. We have posted an incident on our public status page (https://status.redwood.com) and our SREs are actively investigating.

What we know so far:
- Impact: increased tail latency and some 5xx responses for customer requests routed to the us-west cluster.
- Window: started ~06:55 PT; currently ongoing but traffic is degrading rather than fully offline.
- Immediate mitigation: routing policy to failover traffic to the secondary pool is in progress for affected tenants.

Action items for this thread:
1) Can you confirm whether Concordia is seeing timeouts or user-facing errors, and if you have example request IDs/timestamps?
2) We're prioritizing a targeted failover for your routes; we’ll notify you before we flip traffic.

I’ll send rolling updates as we have them. Apologies for the disruption — we understand this impacts your clinical inference jobs.

— Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@concordiahealth.io>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 07:29:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Status page update: Intermittent API latency affecting hosted inference — investigating

Thanks Ava — we are seeing elevated error rates on our side. Sample observed behavior: requests to /v1/generate taking 10-30s then returning 504; patient processing queue is backing up. Example request IDs: req_20260711_0701_8345, req_20260711_0712_1902.

We attempted a retry in our worker, which reduced immediate user-facing errors but queued work increased. Any chance you can provide an ETA for the failover? If you flip traffic, can you confirm it will be zero-downtime on our side or will we need to re-auth/re-establish sessions?

— Alex Mercer
SRE Lead, Concordia Health

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 08:05:43 -0700
Subject: RE: internal: root-cause hypothesis & mitigation for us-west latency

Ava / Marissa —

Quick technical notes from the SRE rotation:
- Symptoms: memory pressure on a subset of serving nodes in the us-west pool combined with an artifact of the batching allocator caused significant stall in the token generation pipeline. That led to request timeouts and high tail latency.
- Immediate mitigation performed: reclaimed caches on affected hosts, increased request-level CPU priority, and applied a temporary routing rule to shift ~40% of traffic to the cold pool.
- Next steps (short window): perform a targeted pool drain of the 6 nodes that showed L3 cache thrashing, push a fix to the batching allocator to prevent the pathological allocation pattern, and continue ramping the failover to 100% if metrics stabilize.

Impact notes for Concordia: the routing change should remove you from the affected nodes with no API key rotation required. We expect ~10–15 minutes of catch-up latency as queues drain.

I’ll coordinate with Marissa for customer comms. If Concordia reports full recovery after the routing change we’ll start the postmortem draft.

— Dev Patel
SRE, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@concordiahealth.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Incident resolved for Concordia — summary and next steps

Alex —

Final update: our teams completed the targeted drain and config change at 08:12 PT on 2026-07-11. The failover routing reached 100% for affected traffic by ~08:20 PT; we observed tail latency return to baseline and error rates drop to <0.1% across your tenant by 08:35 PT.

What we delivered:
- Root cause: pathological batching allocator behavior triggered under a specific memory pressure pattern; two backend nodes experienced L3 cache thrashing.
- Immediate mitigations: cache reclamation, routing failover to cold pool, temporary CPU priority adjustments.
- Permanent fix planned: a patch to the batching allocator (deploy scheduled 2026-07-14) and additional guardrails in autoscaling to prevent overload spillover.

Attached is a short incident summary for your records (incident_summary_concordia_20260711.pdf) and a link to the full postmortem we’ll publish after the internal review: https://docs.redwood.com/postmortems/2026-07-11-concordia-api-latency.

Apologies again for the disruption. Marissa and I are available if you want a short walk-through of the postmortem or to coordinate additional runbook changes for your integration.

Regards,

— Ava Chen
